issues.description: The problem statement / UML and task description specify checkOrderReady() as a void method, but the solution implementation declares checkOrderReady() to return a boolean. This return-type mismatch can confuse students about the required signature and return value semantics and may cause integration/test inconsistencies.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the method signature across artifacts. Either change the solution's checkOrderReady() to have a void return type (and keep any internal boolean behavior private) to match the problem/UML, or update the problem statement/UML to declare checkOrderReady() as returning boolean and explain the meaning of the return value. Ensure the template SealSaloon (to be provided to students) uses the same signature as the corrected specification.
